citation.title: A model-based technique for integrated real-time profile control in the JET tokamak
citation.authors: Laborde L, Mazon D, Moreau D, Murari A, Felton R, Zabeo L, et al.

topic: JET real-time MIMO profile control of q/iota and the ECE-derived rho*_Te profile using Galerkin projection and an SVD-based PI controller
own_question: Can current and electron-temperature-gradient profiles be controlled simultaneously with three heating and current-drive actuators?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors identified a static gain matrix from open-loop JET pulses and projected profiles onto spline and triangular bases. The controller used a weighted pseudo-inverse in a PI loop. Closed-loop pulses (#62156, #62160, #62527) were reported to move profiles toward their targets. Evidence is from a few discharges. The paper reports no forecasting or estimation metrics.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Real-time profile control in JET used ECE electron-temperature-gradient measurements as a sensor for ITB strength.
claim_checks.qualification: This concerns electron ECE, not impurity CES Ti. It is control, not nowcasting.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Real-time ECE and magnetic q reconstruction were used. No CES, BES, ECEI or report-latency handling.
validation_if_relevant: Few closed-loop pulses on one machine. No held-out estimator validation.
forbidden_inferences: Does not support CES nowcasting accuracy
Does not show prior work is noncausal or electrons-only
No timing figure transferable to our 10 ms claim
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional citation only, as background showing that real-time profile control motivates timely profile measurements. Its subject (control on JET with electron diagnostics) is outside our task.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
